questions.question: What does the multiplication rule state for events $A$ and $B$ with $P(A)>0$?
questions.explanation: The multiplication rule rewrites a joint probability using a conditional one: $P(A\cap B)=P(A)\,P(B\mid A)$ whenever $P(A)>0$.
questions.source_support: The definition states $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B\mid A)$ when $P(A)>0$.

option_explanations: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)P(B)$ mislabels a union and uses an unconditional product; the rule concerns the intersection $A\cap B$, and $P(A)P(B)$ (no conditional) holds only under independence.
$P(A\mid B)=P(A)+P(B)$ adds marginals, but a conditional probability is never a sum of $P(A)$ and $P(B)$.
$P(A^c)=P(A)P(B)$ is not the complement rule ($P(A^c)=1-P(A)$) and has nothing to do with the joint probability of $A$ and $B$.
